analysis:
Reviewed the two base_text units of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 806-1611) plus the patch excerpt. The PR is documentation-only: it changes the sampling-defaults table row (head ~1841) and adds a paragraph (head 1864-1871) saying the catalog Qwen3.5-9B, qwen3.5-35b-a3b and qwen3.6-35b-a3b-vl-mtp-mxfp8 builds, which ship no generation_config.json, take model-card thinking-mode defaults (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, presence_penalty 1.5). These come from EngineV2SamplingDefaults.qwen35CardDefaults, bound to the model_type. The supplied units do not include the Swift implementation, so the described change is a behavior claim I could not check against code. The patch hunk lines fall outside the numbered base units I received (base ranges 1841 and 1864 are beyond 1611), so I cannot cite them.

Security relevance: sampling defaults do not touch plaintext prompt handling (A-001), encryption keys, attestation, authorization, or the TB-002 wire contract. No new network, disk or cache surface is introduced. Prefix cache and T-041 behavior are unchanged. A possible interaction for the code reviewer: the default sampling settings feed the complete-checkpoint numerics/identity fingerprint and the serving-profile checks, so changed defaults could alter cache identity or reviewed-profile applicability. The docs claim nothing about this and I saw no evidence of a regression. The base text of the examined units is unchanged context: GLM serving, calibration, deadlines and prefix-cache documentation. I identified no security regression and no threat-model gap requiring an update. Residual uncertainty is low: the Swift change itself was not supplied.
